proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Fix r, r' in R. The local dimension dim_r(R) is independent of the point: the homogeneous lemma gives a field extension k'/k and an isomorphism of the s-fibres over Spec(k') carrying a point over r to a point over r'; by Morphisms, dimension-fibre-after-base-change the fibre dimension is unchanged by the base change, so dim_r(R) = dim_{r'}(R); call the common value d. By Morphisms, dimension-fibre-at-a-point applied with s and with t, dim_r(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{s(k)}(kappa(r)) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{t(k)}(kappa(r)); since both s and t identify k inside kappa(r) the two transcendence degrees both equal trdeg_k(kappa(r)), whence they are equal. Finally, by Properties, codimension-local-ring the dimension of R, and of any open subset of R, is the supremum of the dimensions of the local rings; this supremum is maximal at a closed point r, and for a closed point trdeg_k(kappa(r)) = 0 by the Hilbert Nullstellensatz (Morphisms, Section points-finite-type). Hence d = dim(O_{R,r}) at closed points and dim(R) = d, which gives all four assertions: R is equidimensional, dim(R) = dim_r(R) for every r, the two transcendence degrees agree for every r, and dim(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) for every closed point r. (source lines 1530-1551)

core_obligations: Let r, r' be points of R. First step: dim_r(R) = dim_{r'}(R). The homogeneous lemma provides a field extension k'/k and an isomorphism of R x_{s, Spec(k)} Spec(k') carrying a point over r to a point over r'; by dimension-fibre-after-base-change local dimensions are preserved under the base change, so the transported points have equal local dimensions over Spec(k') and these equal the original ones, giving a common value d. This proves item (1): R is equidimensional. Second step: by dimension-fibre-at-a-point applied to s and to t, dim_r(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{s(k)}(kappa(r)) and dim_r(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{t(k)}(kappa(r)); as s and t both identify k inside kappa(r), both transcendence degrees equal trdeg_k(kappa(r)), proving item (3). Third step: by codimension-local-ring the dimension of R (or any open subset) is the supremum of the local ring dimensions; the supremum is maximal at a closed point r, and there trdeg_k(kappa(r)) = 0 by the Nullstellensatz, so d = dim(O_{R,r}) and dim(R) = d. Hence dim(R) = dim_r(R) for all r, proving item (2), and dim(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) for closed points r, proving item (4).
proof_roadmap: Equalize the local dimensions dim_r(R) for all points using the homogeneous lemma together with the invariance of fibre dimension under base field extension (proof lines 1531-1535).

Apply the dimension-fibre-at-a-point formula with s and with t to get the chain dim_r(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{s(k)}(kappa(r)) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{t(k)}(kappa(r)) and conclude the transcendence degrees agree (proof lines 1536-1543).

Write dim(R) as the supremum of local ring dimensions via codimension-local-ring, maximal at closed points where trdeg_k(kappa(r)) = 0 by the Nullstellensatz, and conclude all four items (proof lines 1544-1550).
